description: Establish a green baseline and reproduce the bug with failing tests before changing behavior. Confirm the existing backend and frontend test suites pass, then add failing regression tests that pin the true root cause of the reported symptom on the BROWSER capture path: (a) scanning the STOCK_IN control barcode in the browser must switch scanner mode rather than create an 'Unknown product' scan entry, and (b) the keystroke-buffering component must assemble a full control barcode into a single onScan call rather than fragmenting it per character. These tests should FAIL against current code and become the acceptance gate for FEAT-002/FEAT-003.
steps: From repo root run `go build ./...` and `go test ./...`; from frontend/ run `npm ci` (or `npm install`) then `npm test -- --run` and `npm run lint`. Record baseline results in findings. If anything is already failing on a clean checkout, note it precisely so later features are not blamed for pre-existing breakage.

Inspect what STOCK_IN_BARCODE.png / STOCK_OUT_BARCODE.png encode. They are Code128 barcodes whose human-readable text is the literal strings 'STOCK_IN' and 'STOCK_OUT'. Document in findings that an HID scanner therefore types the characters S,T,O,C,K,_,I,N then a terminator (Enter), matching the backend defaults STOCK_IN_CONTROL_BARCODE/STOCK_OUT_CONTROL_BARCODE.

Reproduction test A (frontend, control-barcode not recognized on browser path): in frontend/src/components/queue/ScanQueuePage.test.tsx add a test that simulates scanning the STOCK_IN control barcode through the BarcodeInputField (type 'STOCK_IN' into the 'Barcode scanner input' field, then fireEvent Enter) and asserts that NO scan entry POST is made for the literal control string and that the component switches the displayed scanner mode to STOCK IN. Follow existing mocking patterns already used in ScanQueuePage.test.tsx (mock ../../api/client). This test MUST fail against current code (which posts 'STOCK_IN' as a product barcode).

Reproduction test B (frontend, per-character fragmentation guard): in frontend/src/components/scanner/BarcodeInputField.test.tsx add a test that drives the field the way a controlled React input receives rapid scanner keystrokes and asserts onScan is called exactly once with the full assembled string when a single terminating Enter arrives, and is NOT called once per character. Use this to characterize whether the current buffering is correct; document in findings whether the per-character symptom originates in this component's buffering, in a per-character terminator from the scanner, or is purely a consequence of the missing control-barcode classification. Do not over-fit to hardware; keep the assertion about the component contract (buffer until terminator).

Reproduction test C (backend, browser path has no mode switch): confirm via reading code and, if useful, an apitest handlerTestCase in internal/server that POST /api/scans with barcode 'STOCK_IN' currently creates a flagged scan entry (no mode switch, no scanner_mode event). This documents the backend side of the gap that FEAT-002 closes. Keep this as a characterization test clearly labeled; it will be updated in FEAT-002 once the mode-switch endpoint exists.

Write a concise root-cause statement into the feature findings field: the browser capture path (BarcodeInputField -> captureBarcode -> POST /api/scans) never classifies the reserved control barcodes, so STOCK_IN is treated as a product barcode; and separately characterize the per-character fragmentation with evidence from test B.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline command results are recorded in findings: `go test ./...`, frontend `npm test -- --run`, and `npm run lint` statuses on a clean checkout.

New reproduction tests A and B exist and FAIL against current code, demonstrating the bug (control barcode not recognized on browser path; and a documented characterization of the per-character behavior).
findings contains a clear, evidence-backed root-cause statement distinguishing the missing control-barcode classification from any keystroke-buffering behavior.
verification: Run `go test ./...` from repo root to confirm the suite state is understood (record pass/fail).
Run `npm test -- --run` from frontend/ and confirm the new reproduction tests A and B are present and currently failing (red), and all previously-passing tests still pass.
Run `npm run lint` from frontend/ and confirm no new lint errors were introduced by the test additions.

No barcode decoder (zbarimg/PIL) is available in the sandbox, so this is corroborated by three independent sources rather than a live decode: (1) context.json/orchestrator briefing, (2) internal/scanlistener/README.md defaults table, and (3) cmd/server/main.go:137 `envOrDefault("STOCK_IN_CONTROL_BARCODE", "STOCK_IN")` plus internal/scanlistener/mode_test.go cases that use 'STOCK_IN'/'STOCK_OUT' literally. An HID scanner therefore types S,T,O,C,K,_,I,N then an Enter terminator, matching the backend defaults STOCK_IN_CONTROL_BARCODE/STOCK_OUT_CONTROL_BARCODE.

Types 'STOCK_IN' into the 'Barcode scanner input' field and fires Enter, then asserts (a) the displayed scanner mode flips from STOCK OUT to STOCK IN and (b) 'STOCK_IN' is never POSTed to /api/scans. FAILS against current code (mode never switches; the string is posted as a product barcode) -> confirms the bug. This is the acceptance gate for FEAT-002/FEAT-003.

PASSES against current code (see characterization below).

findings.root_cause: The browser scan-capture path (BarcodeInputField.tsx buffers HID keystrokes and fires onScan on Enter -> ScanQueuePage.captureBarcode -> createScanEntry in api/client.ts -> POST /api/scans -> ScanCreateHandler) NEVER classifies the reserved control barcodes. ScanCreateHandler.Handle (internal/server/handler_scan_create.go) unconditionally calls LookupService.Lookup and scan.NewEntryFromLookup, so the literal 'STOCK_IN' is treated as a product barcode; with no product match it becomes a flagged scan entry and the frontend renders it as an 'Unknown product' card. This contrasts with the headless path (internal/scanlistener: handleLine -> classify() in mode.go) which switches in-memory Current_Mode and publishes a 'scanner_mode' SSE event instead of enqueuing an entry. The frontend already subscribes to 'scanner_mode' on GET /api/events and renders a Mode alert, but nothing on the browser POST path triggers a mode switch -- that is the gap FEAT-002 (backend endpoint + shared broadcaster) and FEAT-003 (frontend classification) will close.
findings.per_character_characterization: The reported 'one Unknown-product card per character' symptom does NOT originate in BarcodeInputField's buffering: test B proves the component's contract is correct -- it accumulates every keystroke and fires onScan exactly once with the fully assembled string when the single terminating Enter arrives, and never once per character. Given normal keystroke accumulation the buffering is sound. Therefore the per-character cards are a consequence of the missing control-barcode classification (each assembled control string is posted as a product scan) rather than a buffering defect. The only alternative source would be a scanner physically configured to emit a terminator after every character (one-char-then-Enter), which is a hardware-config path that cannot be reproduced in the sandbox (no physical scanner) and is out of scope; test B guards the component contract so FEAT-003's classification changes do not silently break buffering.
